The story’s architectural metaphors deepen its central conflict: the romance is a charming “folly” that would become “a small, damp house” if made practical, while Clara’s existing relationship has irritations that have become “structural.” These comparisons connect Arthur’s profession to the lovers’ awareness that their intimacy depends on temporary circumstances.
